dr: Probably built late 18th century; police headquarters 1967–1978; museum established 20 May 1991
el: Double-storey fort of rock, coral and mudbrick
te: The fort that became a museum
se: Ajman’s coral-stone fort was bombarded, captured and rebuilt for 200 years, then became the museum of the emirate’s story
sa: حصن عجمان المبني من الحجر المرجاني قُصف واستُولي عليه وأُعيد بناؤه طوال مئتي عام، ثم صار متحفًا يروي حكاية الإمارة
desc: A double-storey traditional fortification of rock, coral and mudbrick in central Ajman, thought to date to the late 18th century. It was the seat of the Al Nuaimi rulers: it was destroyed during the British punitive expedition of 1819, changed hands several times in the 19th and early 20th centuries, and in 1967 became the headquarters of Ajman Police until 1978. After restoration in the early 1980s it became the Ajman Museum, established on 20 May 1991, whose displays include an excavated cemetery from Al Muwaihat with pottery and funerary jewellery dating back as far as 3000 BC. The fort is the centrepiece of the Dhs 25 million Ajman Heritage District, opened in October 2020.
sig: The historic seat of government of Ajman and the emirate’s main showcase of its archaeology and coastal life.

desc: The fort, also called Al Ali Fort, was built in 1768 by Sheikh Rashid bin Majid Al Mualla, founder of the modern Al Mualla dynasty, in the old town of Umm Al Quwain. It was the seat of the rulers and centre of government until 1969, and on 9 February 1929 Sheikh Hamad bin Ibrahim Al Mualla was killed inside it, after which townspeople set fire to its walls. It later served as a police station and was restored and opened to the public in 2000 by Sheikh Rashid bin Ahmed Al Mualla. It now houses the Umm Al Quwain National Museum, whose exhibits include artefacts from the archaeological site of Ed-Dur.
sig: The historic centre of power of Umm Al Quwain and the display home of finds from Ed-Dur.
